desc:
In the integer array nums, exactly two values occur once and every other value occurs exactly twice. Return the two single values as an array [a, b] in ascending order (a < b).

Try to use O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

nums = [1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 5]  →  [3, 5]
nums = [-1, 0]  →  [-1, 0]
constraints: Exactly two values appear once; every other value appears exactly twice
hints: XOR-ing the whole array cancels all the pairs. What is left?
What remains is a ^ b, which is non-zero because a and b differ. Any bit set in it is a bit where a and b disagree.

Pick one such bit, for example the lowest set bit x & -x. Split the numbers into two groups by whether they have that bit set. a and b land in different groups, each pair stays together, so XOR-ing each group isolates one of them.
editorial: Let x be the XOR of the entire array. Pairs cancel, so x = a ^ b, and since a ≠ b, x has at least one set bit. Take the lowest set bit m = x & -x. Exactly one of a and b has that bit, so splitting the array by num & m puts a and b in different groups, while both copies of every other value land in the same group.
XOR-ing each group then yields one single value per group. Finally return the two values sorted. The whole thing is two passes with O(1) memory. A hash-count solution works too but needs O(n) space.
